description_short.value: Non-cumulative, non-voting, irredeemable preference shares of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC, paying a floating-rate dividend each half year.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC 2023 Annual Report (GSE PR 095/2024, note 31(i)(b), non-redeemable preference shares) and the bank's preference share dividend notices on gse.com.gh

description_full.value: These are the preference shares of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC (symbol SCB), which trade on the Ghana Stock Exchange alongside its ordinary shares. They are irredeemable and carry no votes. Dividends are non-cumulative and at the bank's discretion: a dividend that is not paid is lost rather than carried forward, and the holders take no part in any further dividends declared on the ordinary shares. Dividends are announced for each half year, for the periods to March and to September, at a rate that has moved with Ghanaian interest rates, from about 16% in 2022 to 31-34% in 2024. Payments were suspended in early 2022 under a Bank of Ghana directive and resumed later that year. None were paid in 2023, after the government's domestic debt exchange, and the March and September 2024 dividends were paid together in September 2024. The bank's business, board and financial results are those of SCB.
